summary:
Lunar Landing Site Navigator is a tool that helps mission planners evaluate any location on the Moon for a landing. Using real SPICE ephemeris data, it computes the Sun’s and Earth’s azimuth and elevation over time at a chosen latitude and longitude. It combines this with NASA LRO/LOLA digital elevation data to build a local terrain horizon, so it can tell whether the Sun or Earth is truly visible or blocked by terrain, not just above a flat 0° horizon.

For each site, the tool reports LOLA elevation and local slope, a horizon-geometry diagram, a 168-hour timeline graph, and 29.5-day metrics: illumination percentage, longest dark period, Earth contact and blackout duration, and Sun rise/set events. These are combined into a 0-100 suitability score, and everything is exported as a PDF mission timeline report.

This addresses the challenge by turning raw lunar geometry and terrain data into clear, decision-ready information about power (sunlight) and communication (Earth line of sight), supporting safer and better-planned landings.
details:
Lunar Landing Site Navigator lets a user enter any latitude and longitude on the Moon and get a mission-planning report for that site.

How it works: the app uses real SPICE ephemeris data to compute the Sun's and Earth's azimuth and elevation over time at the chosen site. It then samples the NASA LRO/LOLA digital elevation model (about 474 m/pixel) around the site to get the local elevation, the local slope, and a terrain horizon profile. Each body's SPICE elevation is compared with the terrain horizon at its azimuth, so the tool reports whether the Sun or Earth is truly visible or blocked by terrain, not just above a flat 0° horizon.

Outputs: a horizon-geometry diagram, a 168-hour timeline graph with terrain horizon lines, and 29.5-day metrics (illumination, longest dark period, Earth contact and blackout, Sun rise/set events). These combine into a 0-100 suitability score (40% illumination, 35% Earth contact, 25% darkness), and everything is exported as a PDF mission timeline report.

Benefit: it gives mission planners quick, data-driven answers about power (sunlight) and communication (Earth line of sight) for any candidate site.

Limitations: no lunar-limb or refraction correction, and terrain masks depend on the loaded DEM coverage.

Tools: Python, SPICE (SpiceyPy), NASA LOLA DEM, Matplotlib. See the GitHub README for setup.
dataRefs: NASA LRO LOLA Lunar Elevation Data (PDS Geosciences Node)
